parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Sleep Study on Modern-Day Hunter-Gatherers Dispels Popular Notions
parts.article:
Sleep Study on Modern-Day Hunter-Gatherers Dispels Popular Notions
 
(A) The sleep troubles common in modern life have long been blamed on our industrial society, from the city lights, long work hours and commutes, to caffeine and the Internet. Sleep researchers often look back on a time when humans were able to get more rest by sleeping and waking to the rhythms of the sun. It turns out that this may not be quite right. In fact, our ancestors may not have been getting the recommended eight hours of sleep, either. In a recent study, researchers traveled all over the world to examine sleep in some of the world’s last remaining hunter-gatherer societies – the Hadza of Tanzania, the San of Namibia, and the Tsimane of Bolivia. Cut off from media, electricity and other distractions, these pre-industrial societies are thought to sleep the way humans did more than 10,000 years ago. Traveling to where they lived, often in humid, remote locations, researchers used medical devices to record the sleeping habits of 94 of these tribespeople and ended up collecting data representing 1,165 days.
 
(B) They found very similar sleep patterns despite their geographic isolation. On average, all three groups sleep a little less than 6.5 hours a night, do not take naps, and don’t go to sleep when it gets dark. Like many of us, the Hadza, San, and Tsimane spend more time in bed – from 6.9 to 8.5 hours – than they do actually sleeping. This adds up to a sleep efficiency that is very similar to today’s industrial populations.
 
(C) According to Jerome Siegel, director of the University of California’s Center for Sleep Research, evidence suggests sleep habits may not be environmental or cultural, but central to the physical makeup of humans. These findings question the millions of dollars that have been spent on research that tries to explain why some sleepers get only about six hours of sleep a night. Also, such findings question whether lack of sleep is a cause of obesity, mood disorders, and other physical and mental illnesses which have become so common in recent decades. Scientists have documented that people’s energy often falls in the mid afternoon. Some have suggested that it’s because we’ve managed to suppress a natural desire for a nap. However, the new study provides evidence that this is unlikely, and that napping was actually rare in hunter-gatherer societies. The researchers estimated that naps may have occurred on up to 7 percent of winter days and 22 percent of summer days. They noted that their devices were only good at detecting longer naps, so it is possible that some of the study subjects took naps that were short, perhaps 15 minutes or less.
 
(D) Another fascinating finding from the study had to do with the circadian rhythms, our daily activity cycles related to sunlight. Instead of going to sleep right at dusk, tribespeople were staying awake an average of between 2.5 and 4.4 hours after sunset. All three tribes had fires going, but the light itself was much lower than you might get from a light bulb. They did, however, have a tendency to wake up anywhere between an hour before and an hour after sunrise. Siegel and his co-authors investigated this further by looking into the significance of temperature. They found that it also played a big role, though it was somewhat less important than light in influencing sleep patterns. They wrote that “sleep in both the winter and summer usually occurred during the period of cooling and that waking times usually occurred near the height of the daily warming trend.”
 
(E) The tribespeople that were studied are different from people living in modern conditions in a number of respects. Importantly, almost none of them were troubled by sleeplessness. In interviews with the researchers conducted through interpreters, only 1.5 to 2.5 percent of the study subjects said they had severe difficulties sleeping more than once a year. This figure is far lower than the 10 to 30 percent recorded in many industrialized countries today. Siegel suggested that “mimicking aspects of the natural environment” may therefore help treat some sleep disorders. The tribespeople are also much healthier. Not a single one is overweight, indicating their overall higher levels of physical fitness. They also tended to have healthier hearts. Thus comes a critical question. If we can’t blame our health problems on our lack of sleep, could it be that the reason we feel so unrested is because of poor health?

questions.question: Scientists studied hunter-gatherer societies because their sleep patterns are assumed to be similar to those of humans more than 10,000 years ago.

analyses.content: “Assumed to be similar” 对应原文的 “thought to sleep the way...”。
(Paragraph A) “...these pre-industrial societies are thought to sleep the way humans did more than 10,000 years ago.”
题目说科学家研究狩猎采集社会是因为假定其睡眠模式与1万多年前的人类相似。原文A段明确说这些前工业社会“are thought to sleep the way humans did more than 10,000 years ago（被认为睡眠方式与1万多年前的人类一样）”，选 TRUE。

questions.question: The medical devices used in the research were specially designed for humid conditions.

analyses.content: 题目说研究中使用的医疗设备是专为潮湿环境设计的。原文A段只提到地点经常在“humid（潮湿）”的地方，研究人员使用了“medical devices（医疗设备）”，但从未提及这些设备是否“specially designed（专门设计）”用于这种环境，选 NOT GIVEN。
哪怕设备真的能在潮湿环境用，只要文中没说“专门为此设计”，就是NG。不要脑补“能用就是专门设计的”。
(Paragraph A) “Traveling to where they lived, often in humid, remote locations, researchers used medical devices to record...”

questions.question: Researchers found that tribespeople stayed longer in bed than inhabitants of industrialised regions.

analyses.content: 题目说研究人员发现部落居民比工业化地区居民在床上待的时间更长（longer）。原文B段只说部落居民在床上的时间比实际睡觉时间长（组内比较），且其睡眠效率与工业人口“similar（相似）”，并未将两者的“在床时长”进行绝对值的大于小于比较，选 NOT GIVEN。
这是一个典型的比较级陷阱。原文说 “Like many of us... spend more time in bed than... sleeping”（像我们一样，在床时间 > 睡眠时间），这是说两者模式相同，而不是说部落人的在床时间（6.9-8.5小时）比我们的更长。
(Paragraph B) “Like many of us, the Hadza... spend more time in bed... than they do actually sleeping. This adds up to a sleep efficiency that is very similar to today’s industrial populations.”

questions.question: Jerome Siegel believes that environment and culture have little effect on sleep patterns.

analyses.content: “Little effect” 对应原文的 “not be... but...”。
题目说Jerome Siegel认为环境和文化对睡眠模式影响很小。原文C段Siegel指出证据表明睡眠习惯可能“not be environmental or cultural, but central to the physical makeup（不是环境或文化的，而是人类生理构成的核心）”，即主要受生理影响，环境文化影响小，选 TRUE。
(Paragraph C) “...sleep habits may not be environmental or cultural, but central to the physical makeup of humans.”

analyses.content: 题目说科学家记录到了下午____的下降。原文C段提到科学家记录了人们的“energy（精力/能量）”经常在午后下降，填 energy。
“Drop in” 对应原文的 “falls”。
(Paragraph C) “Scientists have documented that people’s energy often falls in the mid afternoon.”
题目说打盹在____期间发生得更多。原文C段提到打盹可能发生在多达7%的冬日和22%的“summer（夏季）”日子里，22% > 7%，即夏季更多，填 summer。
题目是比较级“more often”，原文是数据对比（22% vs 7%）。
(Paragraph C) “...naps may have occurred on up to 7 percent of winter days and 22 percent of summer days.”
(Paragraph C) “...so it is possible that some of the study subjects took naps that were short...”
“May not have detected” 对应原文的 “only good at detecting longer... possible that... took naps that were short”。
题目说设备可能没有检测到____的午睡。原文C段说设备只擅长检测长午睡，所以可能受试者进行了一些“short（短的）”午睡（15分钟或更少）没被测到，填 short。
题目说即使有____光线也很弱。原文D段提到三个部落都有“fires（火/篝火）”燃烧，但光线本身比灯泡弱得多，填 fires。
“Even with” 对应原文的 “had ... going, but...”。
(Paragraph D) “All three tribes had fires going, but the light itself was much lower...”
题目说部落人通常在____前后醒来。原文D段提到他们倾向于在“sunrise（日出）”前一小时到后一小时之间醒来，即日出前后，填 sunrise。
“Around” 对应原文的 “between an hour before and an hour after”。
(Paragraph D) “...wake up anywhere between an hour before and an hour after sunrise.”
(Paragraph D) “...looking into the significance of temperature. They found that it also played a big role...”
题目说科学家发现____对睡眠模式的影响几乎和光一样大。原文D段提到科学家研究了“temperature（温度）”的重要性，发现它也起很大作用（played a big role），填 temperature。
题目用 “almost as much influence” 转述了原文的 “played a big role... somewhat less important than light”（虽然原文说比光稍微不重要一点，但也是big role，在填空题语境下对应最贴切）。
题目说____是极少数部落人遭受的问题。原文E段开头说几乎没人受“sleeplessness（失眠）”困扰，填 sleeplessness。
“Very few... suffered from” 对应原文的 “almost none... troubled by”。
(Paragraph E) “Importantly, almost none of them were troubled by sleeplessness.”
题目说部落人身体素质更好且不____。原文E段提到没有一个人是“overweight（超重的）”，填 overweight。
“Not” 对应原文的 “Not a single one is”。
(Paragraph E) “Not a single one is overweight...”
题目说部落人也有更强壮的____。原文E段说他们也倾向于拥有更健康的“hearts（心脏）”，stronger对应healthier，填 hearts。
“Stronger” 是 “healthier” 的同义替换搭配。
(Paragraph E) “They also tended to have healthier hearts.”
